subject: environmental-science
title: Phosphorus and Water Cycles
welcome_lead: No atmospheric phase, no escape — phosphorus moves with rocks and water.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on phosphorus and hydrological cycles.
final_note: Phosphorus is finite, slow and irreplaceable — a quiet limit on agriculture.

concepts.def: P cycle has no significant atmospheric phase; dominated by rock weathering.
Geological reserve mined in Morocco/Western Sahara (~70% global reserves).
Forecast supply constraint as easily accessible reserves decline.
Combined evaporation from soil and transpiration from plants.
Surface water flow returning precipitation to oceans (~40 000 km³ yr⁻¹).
Atmosphere ~9 days, rivers ~16 days, oceans ~3200 yr.

walkthroughs.body_html: P weathered from rocks dissolves, is taken up by plants, returned by decomposition, and eventually transported to sediments — a million-year cycle.
~71% of land precipitation returns via ET; only ~29% becomes runoff. Forest cover and soil structure modify this partitioning.
Global agriculture depends on phosphate rock fertilisers. Recycling P from manure and sewage is essential for long-term food security.
